labels.label: bprop:laoucapulse

hypotheses.note: g • 0 = 0 for U × {0} ⊆ E and the zero-section iff; weakened (any isometry, any s) for E ⊆ δ⁺⁻¹(U)

hypotheses.paper: product of the round metric on S⁺ and any euclidean metric on ℝ
hypotheses.note: read as the sup product of the chordal metric and lam·|·|, every lam > 0 (penroseDist); the ℓ² (Riemannian) combination and the geodesic round metric are not formalized (refutation transfers by the SCOPE argument: the shear's singular value tends to 0, contracting in every norm)

d ≥ 2 is added for laoucapulse_zeroSection (metric reading on 𝒮) only; for d = 1 the metric reading is false (not_laoucapulseScaledReading_one) and the conformal reading is TRUE in full (laoucapulse_one)

findings: Prop 4.2 (l.857–865) is false as printed for n = 3 in the sup-product metric reading for EVERY euclidean metric lam·|·| on ℝ, not only lam = 1: the fibre rescaling (u,s) ↦ (u, lam s) commutes with a linear isometry and conjugates the two metrics, so Penrose's counterexample at (u₀,4) moves to (u₀,4/lam) (not_laoucapulseScaledReading_two). The ℓ²/geodesic readings fail by the SCOPE transfer argument (not formalized).

The strongest true form (laoucapulse_corrected): for linear g the expanding domain E ⊆ 𝒥⁺ is open with U × {0} ⊆ E ⊆ δ⁺⁻¹(U), U = {a(g,·) > 1}; at (u,0) g expands with every rate < a(g,u) and none > a(g,u), i.e. the 'common factor' remark l.849–851 is correct exactly on the zero section s = 0, where the shear s·∂a of the s-component vanishes. The inclusion E ⊆ δ⁺⁻¹(U) holds for every isometry, any translation part and every s.

For n = 2 (d = 1) 𝒮⁺ = S⁰ is discrete, every self-map is metrically expanding, and Prop 4.2 fails even on the zero section (boost with a(g,u₊) = 1/2, not_laoucapulseScaledReading_one): 'expanding on 𝒮⁺' must be read as the conformal factor a > 1, which is the reading Sullivan's hyperbolicity (l.1625–1627) uses.

For n = 2 (d = 1) the printed statement holds EXACTLY in the conformal reading ('expanding on 𝒮⁺' = a(g,·) > 1), as the set equality E = δ⁺⁻¹(U), for every isometry (translation part allowed), every lam > 0 and every s (laoucapulse_one, isExpandingAtWrt_penroseDist_one_iff): S⁰ is discrete, so near (u,s) the sup metric sees only the fibre, mapped by s ↦ a(u)s + b(u). So 4.2 holds for n = 2 in the conformal reading. For n = 3 it fails in the metric reading (sup product formalized, not_laoucapulseScaledReading_two; the ℓ²/geodesic products by the SCOPE transfer, not formalized). For n ≥ 3 it holds EXACTLY in the volume (Jacobian) reading, not formalized: the differential of g.(u,s) = ([L(g)]u, a(u)s + b(u)) in the product Riemannian volume is lower triangular (conformal sphere block of factor a, fibre entry a, shear s·da + db below the diagonal), so its Jacobian is a(g,u)^d, independent of s, lam and the translation part, while the sphere Jacobian is a(g,u)^(d−1); for d ≥ 2, volume expansion of g at (u,s) ⟺ a(g,u) > 1 ⟺ volume expansion of L(g) at u, i.e. E = δ⁺⁻¹(U) for every isometry and every s (Penrose's SCOPE: 'the statement holds for volume expansion'). That is a non-tautological reading closing the printed equality for n ≥ 3, but it is not the reading l.1660 consumes (Sullivan's property (i) is metric expansion on 𝒮) and it is not formalized. Not a closure of the label: it stays unmarked.

Prop 4.2 is cited exactly once, at l.1660–1661 (Sullivan's property (i) transferred to 𝒥 along Λ̂ × {0} for the trivial cocycle). That use needs only the zero-section form, which is proved (laoucapulse_cover): if the conformal expanding domains U_i of the γ_i cover Λ̂, the open expanding domains E_i on 𝒥⁺ cover Λ̂ × {0}. So the false part of 4.2 is never consumed. Sullivan's 'some fixed round metric in the natural conformal class' (l.1625–1627), read as a Möbius image of the standard metric (automatic by Liouville for n ≥ 4; a reading for n = 3, where every length-2π metric on S¹ is round), is the N-normalised metric pulled back by [h], h ∈ SO₀(1,d); laoucapulse_cover applied to h γ_i h⁻¹ (linear when γ_i is) and [h](Λ̂) gives the transported statement (stated in SCOPE, not formalized).

Prop 4.17's proof (l.1254–1267) does not cite 4.2; the repulsion it uses is governed by the conformal factor a(γ,v₀) = 1/λ > 1, and the claim 'the basin of repulsion of x₀ contains some δ⁻¹(U)' holds for any isometry γ with L(γ)v₀ = λv₀, 0 < λ < 1, without loxodromy (laoucapulse_repulsive_basin); for linear γ, x₀ = (v₀,0) and γ is expanding at x₀ in the metric reading (laoucapulse_repulsive_linear).

Normalisation check (docstring): Barbot's N is the euclidean norm (l.769–771) and v ∈ 𝒮⁺ is (1,u)/√2 (l.775–783; the printed x₀ = 1/2 at l.783 is a slip for 1/√2), so N(L(g)v) = (L(g)(1,u))₀ = lorentzScale and a(g,v) = penroseFactor exactly; the fibre coordinate differs by √2 and the sphere radius 1/√2 vs 1 is a global scale, both immaterial (expansion is scale-invariant; fibreScale absorbs the fibre factor).
questions: 'Expanding' is undefined in the paper. Which notion does the author intend: metric expansion (∃ l > 1, l·D ≤ D∘g near the point), Sullivan's derivative-norm notion, or volume (Jacobian) expansion? Reading taken here: on 𝒥⁺ metric expansion; on 𝒮⁺ the conformal factor a(g,v) > 1 (equal to the metric reading for n ≥ 3, the only meaningful one for n = 2). Under the metric and derivative-norm readings 4.2 on 𝒥⁺ fails for n = 3 by the shear s·da and holds on the zero section; under the volume reading it holds exactly for n ≥ 3 (Jacobian a^d vs a^(d−1)), but l.1660 consumes metric expansion.

labels.label: bprop:admlox

hypotheses.paper: γ loxodromic, v₀ its repulsive fixed point
hypotheses.note: only L(γ)(1,v₀) = λ(1,v₀), 0 < λ < 1; γ any isometry

findings: Contribution only (the label is owned by Flat.Loxodromic, which proves the global basin for loxodromic γ): the step l.1260–1267 holds locally from the eigenvalue alone, with U a ball around v₀ obtained from the chordal identity.

kb_proposals: Once Externals is imported, `boostIsom` resolves to `Causal.Flat.boostIsom : Fin d → ℝ → isom d` and shadows Penrose's `Laoucapulse.boostIsom` (d = 2): qualify it.

A metric statement about 'expanding' maps on 𝒮 = S^{d−1} is vacuous for d = 1 (S⁰ is discrete): read expansion on the sphere as the conformal factor a > 1, and state the metric equivalence under d ≥ 2 (isExpandingAt_lorentzSphere_iff, via connectedness of the sphere).
`isomPenrose` is a group action, proved through the lightlike hyperplanes it transports (Laou.isomPenrose_mul: image of hyperplanes + lightHyperplane_injective); at graduation it belongs in Penrose.
